reason: Flattening a document whose bundle sets a default equal to the IRI of the document's prefix `ex` gives the name `ex:e`, `dn:x` does not resolve, and `_unused_prefix_in_scope("dn")` returns `dn`. A flattened document declares no `dn` prefix for a bundle default that a prefix already binds (spec 3 section 4.1, docs/howto/networkx.md).

Flattening a document whose bundle binds `bb` and the default to one IRI gives the names `bb:x` and `bb:y` and registers `ex` and `bb`. A flattened document spells a bundle default under a prefix the bundle binds to it (spec 3 section 4.1).

Flattening a document whose bundle sets its default to the PROV IRI gives the name `prov:e`. A flattened document spells a bundle default the document already binds, here the built-in `prov`, under that prefix (spec 3 section 4.1).

A bundle under a document with a default and the prefix `ex` registers no namespace and no default for names the document binds, copies a declaration only when it rebinds the prefix itself (renamed `ex_1`), and rejects a document-default name once it sets its own default. A bundle declares only the namespaces it binds itself (#449, HISTORY 3.3.0, spec 3 section 4.1).

After its document adds a prefix, reads a foreign prefix or links the bundle, or after a pickle of either, a stale bundle resolves a string as a fresh bundle with the same declaration would, and the document gives its own answer. A bundle resolves a string as a fresh bundle would after its document's declarations change (#599, #744, spec 7 section 4b.2).

`bundle.unified()` of a bundle named `ex:bn` that only renames `ex` gives a copy that registers `a` and `ex` and writes `prefix ex <http://V.org/>` in PROV-N. A bundle unified alone declares the prefix its identifier uses, as the document binds it (spec 3 section 4.1, #649, #652).

`bundle.unified()` gives a copy with no namespace parent that declares the document's default and prefixes the bundle does not rebind and the bundle's own, and an IRI both scopes bind keeps the document's prefix. A bundle unified alone belongs to no document, so its copy declares everything it read through the document (spec 3 section 4.1, #650, #652).

After `pickle` with a 3.2.3-shaped state, `pickle` with the current state or `copy.deepcopy`, a document's manager still compacts a prefixed IRI and a default-namespace IRI. A manager from a 3.2.3 pickle or a copy builds its URI index on load (spec 5 section 4.4, #691).

`Namespace("", uri)`, `add_namespace()` of a default `Namespace` object and `add_namespaces({"": uri})` each raise an error that names `set_default_namespace`, and they set no default on a document or a manager. A default namespace is set only through `set_default_namespace()` (#649, #668, docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md).

`set_default_namespace()` raises `ProvException` naming the held name and its new reading when a bundle's identifier or a record, or a document's record, would change, and succeeds on a bundle that holds nothing. A declaration that would change a held name is refused (#573, docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md).

`set_default_namespace()` on a document raises `ProvException` with the message that starts `this bundle holds e` when a bundle reads its bare name through the document's default, and the default stays. A declaration that would change a name a bundle holds through its document is refused (#573, docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md).

Adding an equal namespace registers nothing new and writes no rename, a foreign namespace with a taken prefix is registered as `ex_1`, names resolve under `ex_1` only, and an undeclared `ex_2:z` does not resolve. A namespace the model registers itself never shadows a declared prefix and leaves no alias for a prefix nothing declared (spec 3 section 4.1).

A foreign namespace `foo` for an IRI the document binds as `ex` is read as the registered namespace, so `foo:y` resolves to `ex`'s name. A foreign prefix for an IRI the document already binds reads as the registered namespace (spec 3 section 4.1, 3.2.1 HISTORY entry on the resolution cache).

A name in the document's default is rejected in a bundle with its own default, as an identifier and as a datatype, and accepted in a bundle with none. A name in a default namespace that is not the default in scope is rejected (#473, docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md).

A bundle that asserts a name under the prefix `ex` with another IRI than the document's registers it as `ex_1`, both IRIs survive a read back through PROV-JSON or PROV-N, and a later `add_namespace("ex", ...)` on the bundle raises. A namespace the model registers itself never shadows a declared prefix, and a declaration may not change a held name (spec 3 section 4.1, #573, docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md).

`NamespaceManager().valid_qualified_name()` of a name in a prefix-less namespace raises `ProvExceptionInvalidQualifiedName` matching `declare a prefix` and leaves no default, no `""` entry and no registered namespace, while `set_default_namespace()` on a document registers the default under `""`. A default namespace is an explicit declaration, and the model never sets one from a name it is handed (spec 3 section 4.1, #649, docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md). It took over the job of the removed `test_namespace_cache.py::test_a_prefixless_name_is_rejected_when_no_default_is_declared`. The verifier's faults N1 (set the default before the raise), N2 (mint a prefix) and N3 (change the message) fail this test. Only the contrived N5, which keys the rejection on the substring `implicit`, separates the two.

`add_namespace()` of a prefix a bundle's held name uses, with another IRI, raises `ProvException` and registers nothing, a bundle with a different identifier prefix may rebind it, and a document renames a prefix it binds itself to `ex_1`. A declaration that would change a held name is refused, and a scope's own prefix is renamed (#573, spec 3 section 4.1, docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md).

A refused `add_bundle()` (unresolvable name, collision, own document, collision by IRI, an identifier no namespace compacts, a held IRI in an undeclared default) leaves the bundle's identifier, namespaces, parent and the document's bundles and namespaces as they were. A refused `add_bundle()` leaves the bundle as it was (#726, spec 7 section 3.2, HISTORY 3.3.0).

After `copy.copy()` of a bundle's manager, the clone has the same parent as the original, still reads the document's prefix, and a namespace added to the clone is absent from the original. A shallow copy of a manager keeps its enclosing scope and owns its own declarations (#747, #599).

After `copy.copy()` of a manager, a namespace added to the clone leaves the original unable to resolve its prefix or IRI, and the clone still resolves the original's namespace. A shallow copy of a `NamespaceManager` owns its declarations, so adding a namespace to the copy leaves the original unchanged (#747, HISTORY 3.3.1).

`add_bundle()` given a flattened document copies its records and default into the bundle, so the identifiers keep the spellings `a`, `ex:b` and `c`. `add_bundle()` of a document copies the source scope's default and declarations before the records (spec 3 section 4.1).

`add_bundle()` of a bundle that belongs to another document raises `ProvException` matching `belongs to another document` and leaves the target, the bundle and its source document as they were. A bundle is not moved between documents (#649, spec 3 decision N23, docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md).

After `add_bundle()` the identifier's namespace, a foreign `QualifiedName` or a prefix only the bundle declares, is the only prefix the bundle registers, and the document's namespaces are unchanged. A bundle declares only the namespaces it binds itself, and a document keeps its own (#449, #726, spec 7 section 3.2).

`valid_qualified_name()` of a full IRI gives the prefix and URI a scan of the namespaces would give, for single, nested, default, replaced-default, no-match and enclosing-scope setups. An index of the URIs by length gives the same answer as a scan, and an enclosing scope's prefix reads the text as its own name (spec 5 section 4.4, #691, #599).

After a round trip in every target, and after `unified()`, each bundle's namespace parent is its own document's, with no deprecation warning raised. Every bundle reads its document through its namespace parent and not through the deprecated `document` link (#650, spec 5 section 5.3).

`flattened()` and `unified()` of a document with a default and a bundle keep each identifier's spelling and the default, and `unified()` of a standalone bundle warns `DeprecationWarning` and keeps its spelling and default. Every copy `prov` makes into a scope it builds keeps the source scope's default and declarations (spec 3 section 4.1, #652).

For every example document, the attribute-value document and every PROV-N corpus file, `_lookup(prefix, localpart)` on each scope returns each held name as the same object, and `valid_qualified_name(str(name))` resolves it equal and in the same namespace. The readers' one-walk resolution and the model's resolver give the same object for every name a document holds (spec 3 section 3.4).

`_lookup` returns `None` for an empty prefix with an empty local part, for the prefix `_` and for an unknown prefix, returns the default's name for a colon local part, and returns the document's name from a bundle. A prefix the model cannot spell does not resolve, and a bundle reads its document's declarations (#668, spec 3 section 3.4).

After `doc.unified()` the unified bundle holds one record for two equal entities and registers no namespace. A bundle declares only the namespaces it binds itself, also after unification (#449, HISTORY 3.3.0).

`update()` into a fresh document gives the new bundle its source's default and its own prefix `bb`, the two documents are equal, and the target survives the round trip in every target. Every copy `prov` makes into a scope it builds copies the source scope's default and declarations (spec 3 section 4.1).

`update()` of a document with a default and an entity `e` into a document with no default raises `ProvExceptionInvalidQualifiedName` with the undeclared-default sentence and sets no default. A name in a default namespace the target does not declare is rejected, and the target gets no default from it (#473, docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md).
